Assistant Commissioner of Police (ACP) Manasvi Vashishta during a protest outside the Delhi police headquarters on Monday (November 2, 2026). Photo credit: Special Arrangement
The East Delhi Police has announced weekly meetings every Friday to address the grievances and welfare concerns of its personnel. The move comes days after Assistant Commissioner of Police (ACP) Manasvi Vashishta was suspended following a protest by over 100 police personnel outside the Delhi Police headquarters.
According to an order signed by Additional Deputy Commissioner of Police (East District) Vipul Anekant on Tuesday, all branch in-charges must attend a meeting at the Deputy Commissioner of Police (DCP) office at 4 p.m. every Friday. Personnel with unresolved administrative grievances can attend to submit written applications for redressal. Station House Officers (SHOs) and supervisory officers have been directed to inform personnel about this arrangement during daily briefings and roll calls.
The chain of events began with a minor parking dispute outside a salon in Rohtash Nagar, north-east Delhi, on October 23, which escalated into a confrontation between lawyers and police personnel, ultimately leading to Mr. Vashishta’s suspension.
On the morning of October 23, salon owner Rahul Thakur and his wife Sheetal Thakur found a motorcycle blocking their entrance. When they asked for it to be moved, an argument broke out. A group of lawyers allegedly joined the altercation, vandalised the salon and assaulted Rahul and Sheetal, who is eight months pregnant.
The family went to the Shahdara police station to lodge a complaint, accompanied by Sheetal’s sister Shweta and brother-in-law Vijay Bhati. Another confrontation broke out at the station between the lawyers and the salon owner’s family. During the scuffle, one of the men allegedly used a police officer’s nameplate to strike advocate Lalit Bansal on the head, injuring him.
An FIR was registered naming Mr. Thakur and Mr. Bhati as accused. Both have since gone absconding.
The failure to arrest the two accused led to another confrontation between lawyers and police officials. Bar association members claimed the ACP and SHO Arun Kumar had assured them of arrests. When no action followed, advocates approached the Shahdara police station on October 24, where they alleged Mr. Vashishta displayed his revolver and threatened them.
The incident triggered an indefinite strike by lawyers demanding action against the officers. The strike was called off after the ACP and SHO were transferred.
Meanwhile, the police registered a separate case against Mr. Bansal and advocate Amulya Ratan following a complaint by Mr. Vashishta regarding an incident at the police station on October 24.
Mr. Vashishta alleged that 15 to 20 lawyers entered the SHO’s room, misbehaved with him and accused the police of accepting bribes. He further alleged that a lawyer threatened to beat up the SHO and tried to pull him by the hand.
On October 28, the Delhi police transferred Mr. Vashishta to the Special Police Unit for Women and Children and Mr. Kumar to the security unit. The transfers triggered deep resentment within the police force.
On November 2, over 100 police personnel, including several women officers, protested outside the Delhi Police headquarters. A police delegation met Police Commissioner Anurag Kumar to submit five demands.
Following the protest, the Ministry of Home Affairs suspended Mr. Vashishta pending departmental proceedings, barring him from leaving Delhi without permission.
Meanwhile, a fresh order on Wednesday stated that Arun Kumar, the transferred Shahdara SHO, has now been posted to the Intelligence Fusion and Strategic Operations (IFSO) unit.
The latest incident bears similarities to the November 2019 Tis Hazari Courts parking dispute, which escalated into violence between lawyers and cops, triggering a massive protest by over 2,000 police personnel outside the headquarters.
